title: Modulo of a negative day offset
business_name: Rotation slot wrong for days before the reference date
business_cause: Items dated before the reference date land in a negative or wrong rotation slot, because the Java port computes the remainder with a different rule than COBOL.
probable_cause: Faulty Java uses the % operator, which keeps the sign of the dividend, where COBOL FUNCTION MOD takes the sign of the divisor.
technical_cause: COBOL FUNCTION MOD(-11, 7) is 3. Java -11 % 7 is -4. DIVIDE ... REMAINDER and FUNCTION REM in COBOL behave like Java %, so each construct must be mapped separately. Sources are listed in the case README.
business_fix: Compute the rotation slot the way the COBOL program does, so that days before the reference date still fall in slots 0 to 6.
differs_from_case_3: Case 3 loses a sign in storage; Case 6 uses a different mathematical definition of the operation.

sources.name: IBM Enterprise COBOL language reference, FUNCTION MOD (table: MOD(-11,5) = 4, MOD(11,-5) = -4)
Java Language Specification, section 15.17.3, Remainder Operator %
SEI CERT Oracle Coding Standard for Java, rule NUM51-J
